title: From Space to Success: An Exploration of Interior Design Practices for Optimal Learning Outcomes in Higher Education
review_question: How do environmental factors in learning spaces impact student learning outcomes and well-being in higher education? How do collaborative spaces contribute to social interaction and engagement in higher education? How can interior design elements contribute to student wellness and mental health support in higher education settings?
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: A literature review methodology was used to synthesize existing research on the impact of interior design practices on student learning outcomes and well-being in higher education. Specific inclusion/exclusion criteria were not detailed.

synthesis_conclusions: Interior design practices have complex connections with the built environment and student well-being, influencing optimal learning outcomes.
Effective daylighting, acoustics, indoor air quality, spatial layouts, and technology integration are critical for efficacious learning spaces.
Optimal lighting and daylighting enhance focus and productivity, while controlled acoustics promote concentration and information retention.
Improved indoor air quality and indoor plants positively impact student health and well-being.
Spatial layouts that facilitate collaboration and active learning significantly contribute to student engagement and overall academic success.
Biophilic design elements and color psychology profoundly impact the human mind, body, and nervous system, improving student wellness, reducing stress, and aiding mental health.
Evidence-based and student-centered design principles are crucial for optimizing student learning outcomes in higher education settings.
evidence_gaps: The exact practices that allow environmental factors, collaborative settings, and wellness considerations to coexist effectively remain largely unknown to the general public.
Specific design strategies that best support student wellness require more exploration.
There is not enough research on the effects of individual design elements, as the multitude of variables makes for unreliable research and exaggerated conclusions.
The dynamic nature of higher education, with evolving pedagogies, priorities, and student populations, adds complexity to designing functional learning spaces.
There is a continuous challenge for designers to balance current educational practices with the need for future-proof, adaptable, and sustainable university environments.
Research into color psychology is largely not related to interior design, and more studies are needed to truly understand the psychological effects of applying different colors to interiors.
limitations: The review acknowledges that 'not enough research exists on the effects of individual design elements, as weeding through endless variables makes for unreliable research and exaggerated conclusions,' implying a limitation in the depth of evidence available for specific design elements.
